title: SAP Returns and Claims Control Plane
purpose: Explain customer returns and complaints as control chains: physical receipt, ownership, inspection, disposition and compensation are separate decisions that create different documents and postings.
memory_rule: Goods received is not the same as goods owned, and goods owned is not the same as customer refunded.

decision_axes.question: Do goods physically return?
decision_axes.no: Use a commercial claim unless a replacement shipment is required.

decision_axes.question: Do we need condition-based disposition?
decision_axes.no: Lean Returns may be sufficient for a simple receipt-to-stock and credit flow.

decision_axes.question: When do we take ownership of the returned product?
decision_axes.rule: Receipt can first post to non-valuated returns stock. Refund or a follow-up activity that signals ownership can trigger valuation.

decision_axes.question: What happens to the physical product?

ownership_states.meaning: The customer still has the product or it is in transit back. No company stock exists yet.
The product is physically in the company but ownership has not necessarily transferred. Typical when follow-up is Receive into Plant and refund is Decide Later.
ownership_states.sap_note: Non-valuated returns stock is managed as special stock E for the returns order.

ownership_states.meaning: Ownership has transferred to the company, but the product can still wait for final disposition.
The product is moved to unrestricted, scrap, specified stock, another plant or another owned destination.
The product is sent to supplier, customer or repair flow according to the selected follow-up activity.

follow_up_map.title: Receive into Plant
follow_up_map.business_effect: Receive first, then inspect and decide. This is the typical branch for deferred disposition.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Returns delivery and goods receipt; later inspection decides the next step.

follow_up_map.title: Immediately Move to Free Available Stock
follow_up_map.business_effect: Accept the return directly into unrestricted-use stock.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Inspection document, returns delivery and goods receipt into unrestricted-use stock.

follow_up_map.title: Immediately Move to Scrap
follow_up_map.business_effect: Receive and scrap the product instead of reusing it.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Goods receipt to returns stock followed by scrap movement.

follow_up_map.title: Ship to Other Plant
follow_up_map.business_effect: Receive/inspect and forward the product to another plant.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Returns stock transport order; valuation can be required across company-code boundary.

follow_up_map.title: Ship to Supplier
follow_up_map.business_effect: Receive the product first, then return it to a supplier.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Returns purchase order and supplier-return logistics.

follow_up_map.title: Direct Shipment to Supplier
follow_up_map.business_effect: Customer sends the product directly to the supplier; your warehouse is skipped.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Returns purchase order; no company outbound delivery is needed for the customer-to-supplier leg.

follow_up_map.title: Inspection at Customer Site
follow_up_map.business_effect: Inspect before deciding whether the product should return or remain with the customer.
follow_up_map.follow_on: No final logistics action; another follow-up activity must be selected after inspection.

follow_up_map.title: Transfer to Free Available Stock
follow_up_map.business_effect: Move inspected returns stock to unrestricted-use stock.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Material posting to free available stock.

follow_up_map.title: Transfer to Scrap
follow_up_map.business_effect: Move inspected returns stock to scrap.

follow_up_map.title: Transfer to Specified Stock
follow_up_map.business_effect: Move the returned product to a defined target stock such as second-hand stock.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Material posting to configured storage location / stock type.

follow_up_map.title: Send Back to Customer
follow_up_map.business_effect: Reject or finish the return by sending the product back to the customer.

follow_up_map.title: Goods Receipt Quantity Correction
follow_up_map.business_effect: Correct a goods receipt when the quantity physically found during inspection is lower than the posted return quantity.
follow_up_map.follow_on: Outbound delivery without order reference and goods issue for the missing quantity.

follow_up_map.title: In-House Repair (Service)
follow_up_map.business_effect: Hand the returned object from Sales returns into SAP Service repair.
follow_up_map.follow_on: In-house repair and optional goods movement to repair storage location; refund control must be No Refund for the direct repair branch.

refund_controls.title: Decide Later
refund_controls.effect: Do not start customer compensation yet. Inspection and disposition can happen first.

refund_controls.title: Start Approved Refund
refund_controls.effect: For credit, create a credit memo request. For replacement, create a subsequent delivery free of charge.

refund_controls.title: Immediate Refund / Delivery
refund_controls.effect: Create the credit memo immediately, or create the replacement order, outbound delivery and goods issue immediately. Immediate credit requires the product to be marked received.

refund_controls.title: No Refund
refund_controls.effect: No customer compensation is created. Important for branches such as send-back-to-customer or in-house repair.

records.title: Customer Returns / Advanced Returns Management
records.memory_hook: Receive, inspect, decide logistics, decide compensation. Those are separate controls.
records.lead_summary: The Lead-level point is the separation of physical receipt, ownership, inspection/disposition and customer compensation. A product can be physically received into non-valuated returns stock while the company still defers ownership and refund. Inspection splits can send subquantities to different logistical destinations and can also support separate refund decisions.

trace.effect: Select full Customer Returns rather than a pure credit/debit claim or Lean Return.

trace.control: Returns order with reference where available
determined_by: preceding sales order or billing document
trace.effect: Carries commercial history, quantities, pricing context, product and partner data into the return.

trace.control: Save versus release; optional approval workflow
trace.effect: Saving stores the return. Releasing starts subsequent processing; approval can hold follow-on documents until the return is approved.
Brings the returned quantity into company logistics. Physical receipt alone does not prove ownership.
Allows inspection before taking ownership, or valuates the product when the refund/final disposition transfers ownership.

trace.control: Inspection result with optional quantity splits
trace.effect: One returned item can be split into subquantities with different findings, logistical follow-ups and refund decisions.
Creates goods movements, stock transfer, supplier return, send-back, scrap, unrestricted stock or Service repair documents.

trace.control: Credit, replacement, defer or no refund
trace.effect: Creates a credit memo request, immediate credit, subsequent free-of-charge delivery, immediate replacement delivery, or no compensation.
Stock valuation can occur when ownership transfers; billing/FI then records the customer credit while logistics records the physical disposition.
EWM can inspect and execute simple follow-ups; MM/Purchasing owns supplier returns; Service owns repair; APIs expose returns and inspection to external systems.

data_hinges.if_wrong: Wrong quantity, price, tax history or customer context can be copied into the return.
Analytics and policy routing become useless even when the physical return succeeds.
The system creates the wrong logistical branch or requires missing supplier/plant/service data.
Customer compensation happens too early, too late, in the wrong form, or not at all.
Immediate refund and logistics prerequisites can behave differently from the actual physical state.
The sum of disposition/refund quantities no longer represents what was actually received.
Ownership and inventory value can transfer earlier than the business intends.
Individual returned objects or regulated/batch stock can lose traceability across delivery, inspection and repair.

failures.symptom: Returned goods become company-valuated before inspection or commercial acceptance.
failures.trace: Check refund control → product valuation suspension → selected follow-up activity → goods movement/stock state.

failures.symptom: Inspection is complete but the wrong follow-on document is created.
failures.trace: Check inspection split → confirmed follow-up activity → required supplier/plant/storage data → generated follow-up document.

failures.symptom: Customer refund does not match inspected quantity or condition.
failures.trace: Check inspection split quantities → refund determination level → refund code/percentage → credit/replacement quantity.

failures.symptom: Questionable returned stock becomes available to ATP/MRP too early.
failures.trace: Check receiving stock type → valuation state → unrestricted transfer follow-up → storage-location design.

failures.symptom: Return should go to supplier but purchasing document is missing or wrong.
failures.trace: Check follow-up 0005/0007 → supplier and RMA/return-to address → returns PO creation → MM ownership.

failures.symptom: Repair object is not created or cannot be traced.
failures.trace: Check follow-up 0026 → refund control N → serial/equipment prerequisites → Service integration/customizing → repair object.

tests.setup: Return quantity 10: inspect 6 as reusable and 4 as scrap.
assert: refund decision can be traced to the inspected quantities

tests.setup: Receive a product with Receive into Plant and Decide Later.
assert: stock is non-valuated returns stock before ownership decision
final follow-up/refund creates the expected valuation transition

tests.setup: Use Ship to Supplier after inspection.
assert: Sales return remains traceable to MM supplier return

tests.setup: Refund by replacement with a different replacement product and supplying plant.
assert: subsequent delivery free of charge is created

records.title: Lean Customer Returns
records.memory_hook: Receive it, return it to valuated stock, credit it. No disposition engine in the middle.
records.lead_summary: Lean Returns is deliberately smaller. It fits a controlled scenario where goods can go back to valuated stock without inspection-driven logistical follow-up, refund control or supplier/repair orchestration.

trace.effect: Select Lean rather than full Customer Returns.
Anchors the commercial return.
Returned product goes to valuated company stock.
Credits the customer without ARM-style inspection/refund-control branching.

data_hinges.if_wrong: Bad stock can re-enter usable inventory because the lean process deliberately skips disposition logic.
Returned stock can become available to fulfillment sooner than intended.

failures.symptom: Business asks for inspection, supplier return or repair after the lean flow is already chosen.
failures.trace: Re-evaluate process scope; these are signals for SD.RET.ARM, not more custom logic inside Lean Returns.

records.title: Credit Memo Request
records.memory_hook: Goods stay put; reduce the customer's commercial charge through a controlled request.
records.lead_summary: A credit memo request is a financial complaint path, not reverse logistics. The main controls are reference/copying, requested value, billing block or approval, pricing context and release into billing.

trace.effect: Use a credit memo request instead of a returns order.

trace.control: Independent or referenced credit memo request
trace.effect: Copies the relevant commercial context and creates document-flow evidence.
Defines how much revenue/receivable is proposed to be reduced.
Prevents the request from becoming a credit memo before the claim is accepted.
Creates the financial correction in billing and FI without inventory movement.

data_hinges.if_wrong: Tax, pricing and customer context can be wrong even if the credit amount looks plausible.
The request can be financially executed before evidence is reviewed, or remain stuck forever.
A historical claim can accidentally use today's commercial conditions.

failures.symptom: Approved credit request never appears for billing.
failures.trace: Check approval status → billing block → rejection status → billing relevance/copy control → billing due list.

failures.symptom: Credit amount differs from expected claim.
failures.trace: Check reference → copied pricing elements → pricing date/redetermination → quantity → manual conditions.

tests.setup: Create a referenced credit memo request above an approval threshold.
assert: credit memo and FI posting reflect approved amount

extensions: Credit Memo Request A2X OData V4

records.title: Debit Memo Request
records.memory_hook: Goods do not move; increase what the customer owes through a governed request.
records.lead_summary: Debit memo processing mirrors the governance shape of a credit request but the financial direction is opposite. It is for undercharge or another justified additional charge, not for correcting a physical delivery problem.

trace.effect: Use debit memo processing.

trace.control: Independent or referenced debit memo request
trace.effect: Preserves the original commercial context where required.
Defines the receivable increase.
Requires review before billing.
Posts the additional receivable/revenue/tax effect without goods movement.

data_hinges.if_wrong: The customer sees an extra charge with weak traceability.
A correction of old business can use an incorrect financial basis.

failures.symptom: Debit request is accepted but no debit memo is produced.
failures.trace: Check approval → billing block → rejection → billing status/due list.

assert: debit memo increases receivable by the approved delta

records.title: Invoice Correction Request
records.memory_hook: Represent original and corrected invoice values together, then bill the difference.
records.lead_summary: Invoice correction is useful when the invoice itself is the object being corrected. SAP creates paired credit/debit items for each copied invoice item; the user changes the debit side and the system derives the delta.

trace.effect: Use an invoice correction request rather than a physical return.

trace.control: Invoice reference is mandatory to the correction concept
trace.effect: Creates item pairs containing the original and corrected commercial values.
Original value is credited and corrected value is represented on the debit item; the difference becomes the correction.
Holds the correction until accepted.
Corrects FI/revenue/tax without inventory movement.

data_hinges.if_wrong: The wrong transaction is corrected.
The calculated delta has the wrong sign or amount.

failures.symptom: Correction moves value in the unexpected direction.
failures.trace: Compare original credit item and modified debit item; prove the resulting difference before billing.

tests.setup: Copy an invoice item with value 100 and correct it to 90.
assert: resulting customer correction is the 10 delta

records.title: Invoice Increase Request
records.memory_hook: The old invoice is explicitly too low; create the extra debit as a delta.
records.lead_summary: Invoice Increase Request is narrower than a general debit memo request: it is explicitly based on an existing invoice whose quantity or price must be increased, and the follow-on is a debit memo for the calculated difference.

trace.effect: Use invoice increase rather than an unrelated debit request.
Provides original quantity/price baseline.
System calculates the increase delta.
Creates the additional debit only after review.

data_hinges.if_wrong: The increase loses its baseline.
Wrong debit delta is produced.

failures.symptom: Increase request cannot explain the extra amount.
failures.trace: Prove original invoice value → corrected value → calculated delta.

tests.setup: Increase an invoiced item from 100 to 115.

records.title: Free-of-Charge Subsequent Delivery
records.memory_hook: The complaint is resolved with goods, not money.
records.lead_summary: This claim branch creates another outbound logistics flow. It is appropriate for shortage or damaged shipment when the customer needs replacement/additional goods. It should be referenced to the original transaction and normally governed by a delivery block or rejection reason until the claim is accepted.

trace.effect: Choose a free-of-charge subsequent delivery instead of a pure credit.
Keeps the replacement traceable to the failed original fulfillment.
Prevents inventory from leaving before the replacement is approved.

trace.control: Delivery and PGI without normal customer charge
trace.effect: Moves stock and cost while resolving the complaint without normal sale revenue.

data_hinges.if_wrong: Replacement can look like an unexplained giveaway.
Inventory cost exceeds the accepted claim.
Goods can ship before commercial approval.

failures.symptom: Replacement ships with no clear claim evidence.
failures.trace: Check reference → complaint reason → delivery block/approval → replacement quantity → document flow.

tests.setup: Customer received 8 of 10; approve replacement of 2.
assert: no normal customer invoice for replacement

integration_boundaries.ownership: Warehouse execution and optionally inspection / simple follow-up activities
integration_boundaries.handoff: Returns order/delivery comes from Sales; complex follow-up documents can return to S/4HANA Sales/MM/Service for orchestration.

integration_boundaries.ownership: Supplier return purchase order and supplier-return logistics
integration_boundaries.handoff: ARM follow-up 0005/0007 selects supplier branch; Purchasing owns the downstream supplier return.
Sales return decides repair as resolution and transfers traceable repair objects; Service owns precheck and repair execution.
Refund control or claim release creates billing documents and financial postings.
Customer Return A2X V4 handles standard CBAR returns; Returns Inspection A2X V4 handles inspection data and split items. API feature coverage differs between V2/V4/A2A.

lead_answer_frames.question: Explain Advanced Returns Management.
answer_shape: Start with physical return and business reason.
Explain logistical follow-up as the physical disposition decision.
Explain refund control as a separate compensation decision.
Finish with generated documents, integration boundary, one failure and one test.

lead_answer_frames.question: Credit memo request or customer return?
answer_shape: If no goods move, start with a commercial claim.
If goods return, use reverse logistics.
If physical return needs inspection/disposition/refund flexibility, use full Customer Returns/ARM.
If it is a simple receive-to-stock + credit flow, Lean Returns may be enough.

lead_answer_frames.question: When does ownership transfer in ARM?
answer_shape: Do not equate goods receipt with ownership.
Typical deferred returns can first sit in non-valuated returns stock.
Refund or a final follow-up activity that signals ownership triggers valuation unless valuation is deliberately suspended.
